examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
BFS discovers unweighted shortest distances in layers. DFS timestamps form nested or disjoint intervals, never crossing; back edges indicate ancestor connections. A directed graph is acyclic iff a complete DFS finds no back edge. An undirected edge is typically represented twice, so classification must account for the parent edge. Traversing from each unvisited vertex covers disconnected components. Complexity depends on adjacency representation.

**Key relationship:** BFS shortest distance is measured in number of edges, not arbitrary weights

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Fix directedness and neighbour order when required.
2. Record queue layers or DFS discovery/finish times.
3. Run from unvisited roots to cover all components.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: BFS gives shortest unweighted edge-count distances. DFS discovery/finish intervals are nested or disjoint, never crossing. Undirected DFS has tree/back edges under the usual classification; DAGs cannot have back edges. Traversals from each unvisited vertex recover all components.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A BFS tree rooted at s has height 9 in a connected undirected graph. What is the largest possible graph diameter?

**Answer: 18.** For any u,v, d(u,v)≤d(u,s)+d(s,v)≤18. A path of length 18 with s in the middle attains 18, so the bound is tight.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Double BFS computes an exact diameter for trees; it need not compute the exact diameter of an arbitrary graph.

DFS discovery order is not generally a shortest path order.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

Unweighted shortest-path distances are directly produced by:

- **A.** Heap construction
- **B.** BFS
- **C.** Arbitrary DFS tree depths
- **D.** Kruskal

**Answer: B.** BFS discovers vertices in nondecreasing number of edges from the source; DFS depths need not be shortest.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** Adjacency-list BFS is O(V+E)
- **B.** DFS timestamp intervals cannot cross
- **C.** Every DFS tree is a shortest-path tree
- **D.** A directed back edge proves a cycle

**Answer: A, B, D.** DFS can take a long detour before discovering a vertex, so its tree path need not be shortest.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

A BFS source has eccentricity 5 in a connected undirected graph. Maximum possible diameter?



**Answer: 10.** For any u,v, distance≤d(u,s)+d(s,v)≤10. A length-10 path with source at its centre attains the bound.

#### Pattern 4 · NAT · Transfer problem

A directed unweighted graph has edges s→a,s→b,a→c,a→d,b→c,b→d,c→t,d→t. Number of shortest s-to-t paths?



**Answer: 4.** BFS layers are {s},{a,b},{c,d},{t}. a and b each receive one path; c and d each receive two; t receives 2+2=4. All have three edges.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2023 CS · Q56 · NAT

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/graph-traversals?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Breadth-first and depth-first search. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. The power set of {1,2,3} has 2³=8 vertices. The empty set is a proper subset of every other vertex, so it is adjacent to all seven.
2. BFS starting at ∅ discovers those seven vertices in its first adjacency scan. Every one is at distance 1; there are no further undiscovered vertices to constrain their order.
3. All 7! orders are possible, giving **5040**.

#### GATE 2024 CS1 · Q45 · MSQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/graph-traversals?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Breadth-first and depth-first search. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. A forward edge from an ancestor to a non-child descendant would give a shorter root-to-descendant path than its tree depth. That contradicts the tree also being a BFS tree, so C is true.
2. Back edges can return to ancestors without shortening their distances. Directed cross edges can also exist, for example between same-depth vertices visited in an appropriate DFS order.
3. Thus A,B,D are not universal. Select **C**.
